latest_release.name: trigger.dev v4.8.5
latest_release.body:
This is a security release. Update the CLI and redeploy to pick up the fixes.

Most tasks are not affected. The high severity issues only matter if your task code, or a package it uses, runs an HTTP/2 or HTTPS server inside the task. Regular outbound calls with `fetch`, `node:http` or `node:https` (calling APIs, databases or LLM providers) are not affected by them.

## Upgrade

```sh
npx trigger.dev@latest update  # npm
pnpm dlx trigger.dev@latest update  # pnpm
yarn dlx trigger.dev@latest update  # yarn
bunx trigger.dev@latest update  # bun
```

Self-hosted Docker image: [`ghcr.io/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev:v4.8.5`](https://github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev/pkgs/container/trigger.dev/1546615571?tag=v4.8.5)

## Release notes

Read the full release notes: https://trigger.dev/changelog/v4-8-5

## What's changed

## Improvements
- Deployed tasks on the `node`, `node-22`, `node-24` and `node-26` runtimes now run on Node.js 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1, the November 2026 security releases. They fix several high severity issues in HTTP/2 and TLS, including CVE-2026-123863, CVE-2026-123864, CVE-2026-123865, CVE-2026-123866, CVE-2026-123872 and CVE-2026-123874, plus CVE-2026-126051 on Node.js 24 and 26. Existing deployments keep the old runtime until you redeploy with this version. ([`b58c0f9e9`](https://github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev/commit/b58c0f9e9e7b5b78d6a07d0a390f42767201ce42))

## Server changes

These changes affect the self-hosted Docker image:

- The webapp and supervisor images now run on Node.js 24.22.3, the November 2026 security release.

## All packages: v4.8.5

@trigger.dev/build, @trigger.dev/convex, @trigger.dev/core, @trigger.dev/linear, @trigger.dev/python, @trigger.dev/react-hooks, @trigger.dev/redis-worker, @trigger.dev/rsc, @trigger.dev/schema-to-json, @trigger.dev/sdk, @trigger.dev/slack, trigger.dev

## Contributors

Eric Allam, github-actions[bot], Chris Arderne
